title: Prism Split
summary: Split one beam into simple beams by partial fractions: two factors, a repeated factor and three factors, checked by a scanner.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Partial fractions with distinct linear factors
learningOutcome: The student can write a proper rational function as a sum of simple fractions for distinct, repeated and three linear factors, and find each strength by covering a factor or by matching coefficients.

levels.title: Two beams
levels.adds: Baseline: (px + q)/((x − a)(x − b)) = A/(x − a) + B/(x − b); find A and B by covering a factor or by matching (Ex 7.5 Q1 to Q8; Examples 11, 12).
hints: Write the split with unknown A and B and clear the bottoms.
Put x = a to remove B, then x = b to remove A.
Check: A + B must equal the coefficient of x on top.

levels.title: A repeated factor
levels.adds: New: (px + q)/(x − a)² = A/(x − a) + B/(x − a)²; two pieces for one repeated factor (Ex 7.5 Q9 to Q14; Examples 13, 14).
hints: A repeated factor needs one piece for each power.
Multiply through by (x − a)²: the top is A(x − a) + B.
Matching the x terms gives A, then x = a gives B.

levels.title: Three beams
levels.adds: New: three distinct linear factors give three pieces A, B and C, each found by covering its own factor (Ex 7.5 Q15 to Q23; Examples 15, 16).
hints: Cover one factor at a time and put its zero into the other two.
The three strengths add up to the coefficient of the top power.
Put the pieces over the common bottom to check the whole top.

misconceptions: A repeated factor needs only one piece
The strengths can be read off the top
A proper fraction splits into pieces with the same bottom
